event: A TIQUILA customer VXE30 (tail not given) showed visible wing flapping vibration twice during VTOL landing descents; flights were stopped and the aircraft flew normally the next day.
component: VTOL AP attitude (roll) control loop gains, interacting with stiffer newer wing, joiner and lift boom structure
failure_mode: Underdamped left/right lift power oscillation near 8 to 9 Hz during crosswind hover or pause on descent, exciting the wing structure
contributing: newer, stiffer wing assemblies (manufacturing process improvements)
lift boom and joiner tube combinations influence amplitude
light crosswind with yaw hold instead of weathervaning

evidence.quote: The power is oscillating between the right and left sides of the vehicle at a frequency of ~8.7 Hz. To me this indicates an issue with gains resulting in an underdamped system.
I plotted the PSD of the Gyro roll rate and saw a mode at 7.9-8.7Hz across all of the datasets that Jack provided me.
These investigations failed to find a single smoking gun. However, it seems that our stiffer wings and control system are prone to approaching resonance when faced with a crosswind.
The center wing from 300 produced completely smooth hover, suggesting this oscillation is a linked to the mechanical properties of our newer wings.
I agree that it does not appear to be a flight safety concern, but is a gain/clock speed issue that we should be able to sort out.

team_root_cause:
Link to report on prior incident. Behavior caused by combination of controls, wind conditions, and exact decent profile.
https://jenaero.sharepoint.com/:w:/s/EngineeringTeam/EaBzWiraHjVDm8zZr6Ijq4ABL8NWjHFn5Dp2k6VgoPOVAA?e=XPA7mc

would_settle_it.what: ENG-3162 100 Hz burst data: confirm the 8 to 9 Hz roll mode and whether VTOL control gain changes attenuate it

would_settle_it.file: TIQUILA TPTR-59 landing videos and AAR
would_settle_it.what: Customer aircraft tail, wind and descent profile, to confirm the customer event matches the engineering asset findings

reasoning: Swap testing on engineering asset 491 showed the oscillation follows the stiffer newer wing, joiner and lift boom assemblies, and rolling VTOL firmware back from 1.52 to 1.44 changed nothing. Burst data show left/right lift power oscillating at about 8.7 Hz and a roll mode at 7.9 to 8.7 Hz, which engineers read as underdamped control gains. The evidence narrows the cause to the VTOL control loop and structure interaction in crosswind hover, but no single part or gain was isolated or fixed.
notes: The detailed testing was done on engineering assets 490, 491, 507 and others (ENG-3162), not on the TIQUILA aircraft; it is applied here by the team as the same phenomenon. Two copies of the same Wing Vibration Report (VA-389 and ENG-3162) are identical. Investigation moved to VXEP-104, which was canceled with no work.

Quality Control Issue.

event: Aircraft 510 with D450XR fuel cell SN 249 had a fuel cell fault (19472, reactor temperature unexpectedly high) in the launch wizard and again right after launch; it was commanded to RTB and recovered.
component: D450XR fuel cell fuel control: fuel solenoid or FMS fuel flow sensor
failure_mode: Over-fueling (fuel solenoid PWM creeping up without matching FMS flow) raised reactor temperature above 850 C for 30 s, triggering fault 19472
contributing: cathode blower running near maximum RPM with little cooling margin (cathode unit also replaced)
high ambient fuselage temperature (about 44 C) on the ground before forward flight

evidence.quote: This is observed in attached data files, as system exceeds 850°C for continuous 30 seconds.
Additional Validation is required to certify the failure point; however, it is clear from functional run data that either Fuel Solenoid or FMS sensor is not functioning properly.
Results indicate that defective Fuel Sensor resulted in likely over fueling resulting in increased temperatures exceeding Cathode functional range.
After CAs implemented, Fuel Flow reacted as intended and temperature control was maintained.
I want to issue an RMA for this fuel cell so that I can examine some of the likely root causes for this failure mode; notably the Fuel FMS, Cathode Interface, & the stack Heat Exchanger.

team_root_cause: Poor performance of Fuel Sensor or Solenoid.

would_settle_it.file: Bench test of removed fuel solenoid and FMS sensor
would_settle_it.what: Test each removed part separately to show which one caused the PWM creep and over-fueling
ENG-3064 cycle data plot showing the temperature step between cycles 6 and 7

reasoning: The fault flight data show reactor temperature over 850 C for 30 s with the cathode blower near its limit. Bench runs did not reproduce the fault, but fuel solenoid PWM crept far above normal at constant reported flow, pointing to over-fueling from either the fuel solenoid or the FMS sensor. Replacing both parts (and the cathode unit) restored steady fuel PWM and temperature control, so the cause is narrowed to the fuel control pair but not to one part.
notes: The report names the fuel sensor in its conclusion but replaced the fuel solenoid, FMS sensor and cathode unit together, so no single part was isolated. Ticket status Canceled though the report is complete. Fuel cell is written as 249, 4006249 and D4500249. Records were mixed up with VXEP-31 (TPTR-58). Fuel cell CSV summaries hold only headers; the combined run data xlsx is raw rows and was skimmed.

event: During TIQUILA STALKER FAT, the main and hybrid lift battery chargers would not charge from a 12 V DC supply, showing "input voltage lower than 12.6V".
component: ISDT Q8 Max battery charger custom firmware, minimum input voltage setting
failure_mode: Minimum input voltage locked at 12.6 V (car battery, engine running value); the change to 10.5 V requested in 2022 was never applied
contributing: charger settings locked in custom firmware, user cannot change
SRD-186 requires charging from a 12 V supply

evidence.quote: Under system settings, I was able to find that the “Lowest input voltage” is set to 12.6. I wasn’t able to change it.
Confirmed, we never actually updated the min voltage.
Change storage voltage to 3.9, minimum input voltage to 10.5V
Adjusted input voltage (output of power supply) to >12.6V cleared the problem.
Previous software customization document listed 12.6V min (car battery engine on) and 50A max.

team_root_cause: Manufacturer “Lowest input Voltage” is set to 12.6V and therefore the power supply cannot go lower.
reasoning: The error was reproduced in Bend and cleared when supply voltage was raised above 12.6 V. The charger system settings show the lowest input voltage set to 12.6 V and locked. The email history shows a 2022 request to ISDT to lower it to 10.5 V that was never carried out, so the charger configuration, not the power supply, caused the failure.
notes: The team Root Cause says the manufacturer set 12.6 V; the linked ticket shows the 12.6 V value came from Edge's own earlier customization spec and the requested change was never confirmed. Workaround used: FSK inverter plus AC power supply. VA-935 closure report was canceled with no work.

event: During TIQUILA STALKER FAT on a D450+ fuel cell start up, the GCS displayed the fuel cell fan RPM incorrectly.
component: GCS fuel cell control dialog, fan RPM gauge
failure_mode: Gauge range set for older fuel cells; D450+ firmware now reports actual fan RPM (about 3 times the old value), so readings above 10,000 RPM pin the gauge in the caution range
contributing: D450+ fuel cell firmware changed fan RPM reporting without matching GCS gauge update

evidence.quote: D450+ FW now reports “actual output” for fan RPM. It was previously reporting ~1/3 the output (per @Sean Wendling )
When fan RPM exceeds 10,000 RPM, indicator remains at top of dialog in caution range.
At this point the settings on some of the gauges change based on the FC type (first 2 digits of Serial number).
We should verify that https://jenaero.atlassian.net/browse/GCSS-77 is the problem this issue is referencing.

would_settle_it.what: GCSS-77 screenshot of the fan RPM gauge, to confirm it matches the FAT observation

reasoning: GCSS-77 explains that D450+ firmware began reporting the true fan RPM, about three times the old value, while the GCS gauge limits were still set for older units and pinned above 10,000 RPM. The fix was released in GCS software on 3/26/2024 and the incident closed. Nobody wrote down a check that GCSS-77 was the exact FAT observation, so confidence is medium.
notes: No Root Cause field. VXEP-14 (cathode blower failure on D450+ SN 510) is linked as related; its 8D covers blower hardware and software, not the GCS display, so it is not the cause here.

event: During TIQUILA FAT on aircraft 511 (about 7 August 2023), HLB 2-1803 read about 80 percent on the GCS while a battery checker read 98 percent; the same battery was later used in the ENG-2181 aborted launch.
component: Center wing 511 HLB input power connector (AS150 contact), with HLB 2-1803 positive socket
failure_mode: Overheated, high resistance HLB power connection (solder blob, 195 uohm contact, battery socket missing retention ring) giving intermittent connection and low voltage readings under load
contributing: previously damaged center wing 511 returned to service without red tag or RMA update
HLB 2-1803 set aside after a low voltage report but not marked and reused
launch wizard may not update the HLB serial when the battery is swapped, so logs may not be from 2-1803

evidence.quote: CW input power connector showed a solder blob at the base of the contact, which indicates overheating.
Contact impedance measures 195uohms, which is over the newly established criteria of 180uohms.
The positive terminal looks like it is missing the ring around the socket, which could lead to higher contact resistance.
Post flight discharge test appears normal. Indicates no permanent failure in the battery. Issue is suspected to be due to CW511 damage.
However, it should be made clear that the launch wizard likely does not update the HLB # when the step has been passed and the HLB is replaced.
The drop in voltage looks more like battery disconnected vs the description saying 80% SOC.

team_root_cause:
- HLB 2-1803 was used with a center wing that was previously damaged, in engineering for troubleshooting, and should not have been flown or delivered to the customer. The findings were reported in JIRA, but wing was not red tagged. 511 RMA was not updated to indicate connector damage.
- Initial damage https://jenaero.atlassian.net/browse/VA-35
- FAT incident https://jenaero.atlassian.net/browse/ENG-2181 .
- This damage to the connector likely caused the intermittent connection and lower voltage readings.

would_settle_it.what: Line up XCOMM HLB cell total voltage with VTOL Vbatt at the moment the GCS showed about 80 percent, and confirm the HLB serial in the log
Nadia Brown data review slides (SharePoint) comparing cell voltages with flight Vbatt
ENG-2181 photo of HLB 2-1803 positive socket missing retention ring and solder traces

reasoning: The battery checker and a post-incident discharge test showed HLB 2-1803 itself was healthy, while the 511 center wing input power connector had a solder blob from overheating and a 195 uohm contact, over the 180 uohm limit, and the battery positive socket was missing its retention ring. A bad connection explains a low voltage reading under load with good cell voltages. The data review never cleanly matched the 80 percent reading to a log with the battery serial, so this stays narrowed to the connector pair rather than proven.
notes: The raw VTL and XCOMM xlsx log dumps in VA-400 are cut at 150000 characters and were read only for headers and structure, not row by row; the charger and B1 CSV files are raw data. Ticket status Canceled. Center wing labelling is confused across tickets (VXEP-12 calls it 516 CW; VA-35 and this ticket say CW 511). The same battery and wing were in the ENG-2181 abort on 8 August.

event: During TIQUILA STALKER FAT radio testing, after encryption was disabled the platform status output took 12 s to change on the GCS against an expected 5 s.
component: Silvus radio network reconfiguration (encryption mode change)
failure_mode: Normal Silvus reconfiguration time of about 12 s when switching from encrypted to non-encrypted, longer than the 5 s expected in SRD-309
contributing: requirement latency value did not account for radio reconfiguration time

evidence.quote: They now understand that the 12 seconds is the standard operational time required for the Silvus radio to reconfigure the network from encrypted to non-encrypted communications.
THis can’t be addressed it is inherent in the Silvus design.
The expected lag time was 5 seconds however after disabling encryption, the platform status output change was observed after 12 seconds

team_view_in_comments: THis can’t be addressed it is inherent in the Silvus design.
reasoning: The delay only appeared when encryption was switched off, and the vendor review explained that the Silvus radio needs about 12 s to rebuild the network in that case. Nothing was broken; the system behaved as designed and the 5 s expectation in the requirement was the mismatch. The explanation rests on the radio vendor and PTR board statement, not a separate measurement, so confidence is medium.
notes: No Root Cause field. GCSS-83 was canceled with no work. Plan says the requirement may need adjusting.
